$comment: What the weekly health check watches that no package manager knows about.
Runtimes are looked up against endoflife.date at run time rather than
written down here, because a support date copied into a repo is wrong the
first time it moves and nobody notices. Only which cycle we are on is
recorded; the date it dies is asked for each week.
Credential dates are the opposite: no API can tell us when somebody last
rotated a token, so it is written down by hand. A null date means nobody
has recorded one - which is reported but never opens an issue on its own,
since a weekly alarm about a form nobody filled in is how people learn to

credentials.name: BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN
credentials.where: Vercel → Storage → the Blob store → Settings → Rotate Credentials
credentials.note: Rotate; never create a new store. Rotating regenerates credentials on the same store, so the photo URLs already saved in recipe.imageUrl keep resolving - a new store means a new store id and every one of them 404s. Vercel updates the variables it manages and offers to delay the old secret's expiry: take the shortest delay, because the point of rotating is that the old one stops working. Check that the variable the app actually reads was among the ones updated, then redeploy - the new value does not reach the running deployment until you do.

credentials.name: TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN
credentials.where: Twilio console → Account → API keys & tokens

credentials.name: RESEND_API_KEY
credentials.note: Sending access only; it never needs more. Create the replacement before revoking the old one - they coexist, so there is no window where a password reset cannot be sent. Set it in Vercel and redeploy: the value is read into the build, so saving it on a running deployment changes nothing. Note that the domain verification is separate and survives a rotation.

credentials.name: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
credentials.note: Rotating this signs everybody out. Worth doing rarely and deliberately.
